title: An exact computer-assisted lower bound for Fisher-information convexity along the two-dimensional heat flow
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the sharp constant in the differential inequality \[
  I(t)I''(t)\geq c\,[I'(t)]^2 \] for Fisher information along the probability-normalized heat flow on $\mathbb R^2$. The unrestricted log-convexity value $c=1$ is false in two dimensions, whereas the known square-root convexity theorem gives the universal value $c=1/2$. We construct an exact, machine-verifiable sum-of-squares certificate proving the stronger universal bound \[
  c\geq \frac{231691}{250000}=0.926764. \] Together with an independent exact Fourier/Gaussian-envelope construction, this gives \[ 0.926764\leq c_*<0.94176665012062, \] where $c_*$ is the sharp constant for positive-time Gaussian convolutions of arbitrary probability measures on $\mathbb R^2$. We formulate the proof in explicit two-dimensional index notation. The lower bound follows from an exact rational polynomial identity involving a strictly positive denominator, a weighted total derivative, and eleven positive rational Gram matrices. All $491$ recorded leading principal minors are strictly positive and the complete polynomial identity has zero residual. No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption is imposed on the initial measure. The sharp value remains open.

title: Heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause Dynamics Need Not Converge
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20783v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give a six-agent counterexample to convergence of scalar heterogeneous Hegselmann--Krause dynamics.

title: Precise Asymptotics for Dense High-Dimensional Huber Regression under Heteroscedasticity
authors: Jing Zhou, Ramji Venkataramanan, Hui Zou
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20798v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study Huber regression in a heteroscedastic linear model in the proportional regime $n/p \to \delta \in (1, \infty)$. Our main result is an exact characterization of the asymptotic empirical distribution of the Huber estimator. This characterization is in terms of three scalar parameters which determine the first-order centre and the asymptotic variance of the Huber estimator. The result shows that with heteroscedastic noise, the first-order centre may contain an additional component along the variance index coefficient. We derive the displacement coefficients that determine this centre, as well as the exact asymptotic variance. The analysis uses the matrix approximate message passing (AMP) framework to jointly track the regression and variance index coefficients, extending the existing framework for homoscedastic M-estimators. We illustrate the implications of this characterization by constructing a test for centre displacement and examining its empirical size and power through simulations.

title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
authors: Ibrahem G. Ameen, Magda Hammad, Mohsen Razzaghi, Mahmoud A. Zaky
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20829v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.

title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
authors: Wentao Yu, Vincent W. S. Wong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20841v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
authors: Felix Parker, Danielle A. Ripsman, Emmett Springer, Kimia Ghobadi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20892v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learned warm starts for the simplex method build starting bases using predictions of which variables will be basic at optimality. Prior work has shown that starting bases predicted by graph neural networks can sharply reduce iteration counts, but the time saved may fall well short of the iterations saved. On 25 classes of linear programs (LPs), we find that a strong supervised basis predictor removes two thirds of the dual simplex's iterations but only a third of its time. Two effects explain the gap: the iterations removed by a good start tend to be cheap, and closeness to an optimal basis does not rank starts by cost. We prove that two starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis and equal pivot counts can differ in linear-algebra work by a factor that grows with the square root of the number of rows. Empirically, across the starts of one LP, the pivot count explains 71% of the variance of log solve time, while the CPU instruction count explains 98.5%. We introduce CostStart, which uses supervised prediction for the basis and trains a small policy on measured instruction counts to choose, per LP, how many predicted columns to use, which algorithm and pricing rule to run, and whether to warm-start at all. On unseen LPs of the training classes, including LPs four times the training size, CostStart roughly halves the solve time relative to the solver's default start and is 1.4 to 2.2 times as fast as two published methods retrained on the same data.

title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
authors: Chris Verhoek, Charis Stamouli, George J. Pappas, Nikolai Matni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible. We set a first step toward such a theory by presenting a framework for co-designing a two-layer LCA for a linear time-invariant plant. The resulting co-design problem optimizes over architectural design variables (e.g., reduced order model dimension and sampling ratio between the layers) and tuning-based design variables (e.g., the numerical values of the feedback gain or the matrices of the reduced order model), all subject to constraints that ensure stability, feasibility, and compute properties of the closed-loop LCA. The proposed formulation allows to make informed tradeoffs along the Pareto front traced over different axes of optimality, e.g., speed, accuracy or computational effort. We demonstrate the effect of making various tradeoffs in a simple numerical example.

title: Factor-Assisted Density Estimation: When Ambient Dimension Enables Oracle Rates
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20944v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study density estimation in the high-dimensional factor model, whose fixed-dimensional latent factors have an unknown smooth density. We propose factor-assisted density estimation (FADE), a non-iterative procedure that applies kernel density estimation to spectral estimates of the latent scores. The score proxies are dependent and do not follow the latent density, so standard kernel-density arguments do not apply. A refined rowwise expansion separates error into a conditionally centered Gaussian perturbation and a uniformly controlled remainder. We show that FADE achieves the oracle rate in sufficiently high ambient dimension and prove a minimax lower bound separating ordinary nonparametric difficulty from a Gaussian deconvolution obstruction. Together, the upper and lower bounds establish rate optimality of FADE in specified high-dimensional regimes. We also derive $L^1$ upper and lower bounds for the induced observation density, distinguishing latent-distribution uncertainty from the cost of estimating a growing number of parameters. These results formalize a blessing of ambient dimension: sufficiently many observed coordinates can make a simple spectral reduction statistically lossless even for the nonparametric task of recovering an unobserved low-dimensional density.

title: Emergence of partially hyperbolic skew-products with circle fibers
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the statistical behavior of partially hyperbolic skew-products over Axiom A diffeomorphisms using emergence. Generically, these systems satisfy the Palis conjecture: they have a finite number of physical measures whose basins together have full volume. In particular, for Lebesgue almost every point, the empirical measures converge to one of finitely many physical measures. We study the non-generic case and prove that, even when the sequence of empirical measures may have uncountably many accumulation points, these systems have low emergence.

title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
authors: Yifan Wang, Josip Tambaca, Suncica Canic
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes.
  We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.

title: $\lambda$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
abstract:
arXiv:2610.20972v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $\lambda$-geodesically convex (possibly with $\lambda \leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions. We also present some consequences of this result in the study of the sliced-Wasserstein flow.

title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
authors: Namhyun Kim, Sadjad Alikhani, Ahmed Alkhateeb
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21014v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

title: Stationarity equations for fractional affine area measures: ellipsoid rigidity and polytopal solutions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Xi and Zhao established a first variation formula for affine inequalities involving radial mean bodies, and asked two geometric questions about the resulting stationarity equation: whether the bodies already known to satisfy it are the only ones, and whether its smooth solutions are exactly the ellipsoids. We answer both. Every strictly convex solution of the equation with $q>-1$, $q\ne0,n$ is an ellipsoid, which answers the second question affirmatively while replacing smoothness and everywhere positive Gauss curvature by strict convexity. Every full-dimensional facet-transitive polytope satisfies the equation, and so does the polar of every vertex-transitive polytope with respect to its volume centroid; the rhombic dodecahedron, the thirteen Catalan solids and the bipyramids over regular polygons other than the octahedron provide infinitely many affinely inequivalent solutions that are not affine images of regular polytopes or balls, so the answer to the first question is negative. The rigidity proof compares overlap integrals along a continuous Steiner path: stationarity forces an increase of order $o(t)$, whereas a nonaffine chord midpoint function forces an increase of order $t$. For negative parameters the required comparison rests on a minimization formula over bounded measurable auxiliary sets.

title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In stochastic (strongly) convex optimization, establishing last-iterate convergence guarantees for first-order methods has recently garnered increasing attention, as this not only deepens the theoretical understanding of these algorithms but also aligns more closely with practice. Notably, people have demonstrated that one of the most famous, simple, and popular methods, Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\mathtt{SGD}$), provably achieves last-iterate convergence. However, the existing results may have limited applicability, since they typically rely on strong conditions on the gradient noise (e.g., an exponentially decaying tail) rather than the more realistic heavy-tailed noise. Unfortunately, when faced with heavy-tailed noise, $\mathtt{SGD}$ is known to exhibit undesirable behavior or even fail to converge. To address the challenge of heavy-tailed noise, people have proposed $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$, an algorithm that combines $\mathtt{SGD}$ with a simple mechanism, gradient clipping. Although $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ performs well in practice, its last-iterate convergence property remains highly underexplored. In this work, we prove the first optimal last-iterate rates in high probability for $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ under heavy-tailed noise, thereby closing a gap in the literature.

title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
authors: Xuan Li, Kaile Qiu, Chaobao Huang, Weiping Bu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21056v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies numerical methods for the time fractional diffusion-wave equations with the constant delay. Using a symmetric fractional-order reduction technique and introducing the auxiliary variable $w$, we reformulate the original problem as an equivalent coupled system and for the first time carry out a rigorous regularity analysis of $w$. Based on the symmetric graded time mesh, the coupled problem is discretised by the $L1$ scheme in time and a standard finite element method in space, and the stability result of the developed fully discrete finite element scheme is established by means of a discrete fractional Gr\"onwall inequality. Furthermore, we derive a new comparison principle and reconstruct a new barrier function on each interval $((k-1)\tau,k\tau]$, $1\le k\le K$ according to the properties of the symmetric graded mesh. Based on the new barrier function, we obtain new relevant properties, which lead to a novel and crucial stability property for the discrete fractional operator. Combining the obtained local truncation error in time gives a local error estimate for the fully discrete finite element scheme, which shows that our convergence result provides a unified framework that seamlessly encompasses both pointwise-in-time error estimates on uniform meshes and global-in-time error estimates on symmetrical graded meshes. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
authors: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks for PDEs: Structure-Aware Feature Redistribution and Residual-Driven Block Enrichment
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21077v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Randomized neural networks retain an output-linear least-squares solve, but globally sampled random features may fail to capture the spatial and scale structure of PDE solutions. We propose SFRBE--RaNN, a two-stage adaptive trial-space construction. SFR redistributes a fixed feature budget according to regional indicator masses and adapts regional weight scales through low-dimensional residual-based optimization. RBE constructs nonredundant enrichments by screening multiple activation families, removing represented response directions, and selecting the smallest admissible prefix. For solution-dependent operators, candidates are screened with a frozen operator and accepted only after nonlinear residual verification. For fixed linear problems, we establish an exact discrete residual-reduction identity and a conditional solution-error estimate. Building on this identity, we combine safeguarded SFR with RBE capture factors to derive a finite-horizon error bound involving baseline best approximation and empirical consistency, together with a conditional random-search success-probability bound. Numerical experiments on localized, multiscale, and nonlinear space--time problems demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

title: Quantum Color Newton Rings
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21102v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study integral Newton rings attached to symmetric quantum colors. We show that their boundary values at a deleted node are exactly the elements of Habiro's cyclotomic completion, and we describe their quantum neighborhoods at $q=1$ uniformly in the rank. The symmetric-color $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ invariants of a knot are the values of an element of such a ring. In its expansion at $q=1$, the coefficient of $(q-1)^m$ has denominator dividing the $(n-1+2m)$th power of the Alexander polynomial, with integral numerator, and this exponent is sharp. For $5_2$ and $6_1$ at $q=i$, the period matrices of the rank-two coefficient recurrences have spectral modules of exact order three in the Picard group of an affine elliptic curve.

title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization
authors: Hanuka Eshima, Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Andrea Paudice
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We revisit McDiarmid's inequality, a central tool in statistical learning theory and algorithm analysis. We show that large deviations above the mean are exponentially unlikely for functions of independent random variables that are almost surely bounded above and satisfy a conditional moment assumption of order $p\in(1,2]$. When $p<2$, the result applies even when the function has infinite variance. Our proof relies on a new tensorization inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence, termed reverse KL tensorization, which may be of independent interest. Applications include concentration of the sample mean and median-of-means estimator, and one-sided uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.

title: The best Ulam constant of the n-th order linear differential operator with constant coefficients
authors: Jawad Boutarfass, Iz-iddine EL-Fassi, Lahcen Oukhtite
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21122v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space over the field $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}\}$, and let $L:\mathcal{C}^{n}(\mathbb{R},X)\to\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R},X)$ be the $n$-th order linear differential operator defined by $Ly := y^{(n)} + a_1 y^{(n-1)} + \cdots + a_n y$, where $a_1,\ldots,a_n \in \mathbb{K}$ are fixed scalars and $n$ is a fixed positive integer. It is well known that $L$ is Ulam stable if and only if its characteristic equation has no roots on the imaginary axis. In this paper, we determine the best Ulam constant of $L$ under this condition, for an arbitrary order $n$ and without any restriction on the multiplicities of the roots of the characteristic equation. This improves and completes several known Ulam stability results for this operator and provides the best estimate possible for the error between approximate and exact solutions of the equation $Ly=f$, where $f\in\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R},X)$. Moreover, as an auxiliary result, we give an explicit formula for the general solution of this equation.

title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used upstream of decision-making to clean data, detect label errors, and reconstruct missing values. Yet LLM-assisted data curation creates a new operational tradeoff: higher-fidelity models and richer prompts can be substantially more expensive, while the value of this additional fidelity depends on the downstream optimization accuracy. This raises the central question of this work: when should one pay for a better LLM, given a specific downstream task at hand?
  We study this question through stochastic optimization with mixed-fidelity first-order oracles, which can have systematic bias and state-dependent variance. We develop two cost-aware algorithmic frameworks that allow adaptive switching between stochastic oracles. With known bias, the first meta-algorithm applies a restarted, cost-aware policy that adaptively selects oracle fidelity across optimization stages. Its cumulative cost is no larger than that of the best fixed oracle in hindsight and can be substantially smaller. With unknown bias, we develop a budgeted certification scheme that uses occasional trusted-gradient evaluations to certify the optimization progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources, and show an explicit tradeoff between certification cost and delayed detection of biased sources. We provide concrete realizations of these meta-algorithms by applying biased stochastic gradient extrapolation (SGE) and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise as subroutines. Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments illustrate the qualitative switching behavior predicted by the theory: the adaptive policy skips several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reduces cumulative cost relative to fixed high-fidelity alternatives while achieving comparable accuracy.

title: Conditional limit laws for open intermittent dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We obtain conditional limit theorems for open intermittent Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti (LSV) maps. Unlike the results of closed systems (e.g. some uniformly expanding maps), we obtain a new limit distribution, which is different from the Gaussian law or the stable law, for both "regular" and singular observables.

title: Four-Level Quantized Soft Information Aided Hard-Decision Decoder for Product-like Codes
authors: Xiaowei Wu, Min Qiu, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a novel low-complexity soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product-like codes, termed iterative bounded-distance decoding (iBDD) with graded scaled reliability and bit-flipping (GSRF). This scheme operates on four-level quantized soft information. It incorporates a graded scaled reliability rule to assign decoding confidence to the bounded-distance decoding result, and employs a bit-flipping rule based on bit-level and component-code-level reliability. A selective re-decoding rule is designed to further facilitate the error performance while keeping the number of BDD attempts in reasonably low levels. The decoding parameter design of iBDD-GSRF is investigated for product codes and staircase codes, respectively. Simulation results on both codes verify that iBDD-GSRF achieves a gain of more than 0.4 dB over the conventional iBDD, comparable to several existing unquantized soft-aided decoders.

title: A geometric criterion for the dimension of Morgan-Scott spline spaces $S_{2r}^r(\Delta_{\mathrm{MS}})$
authors: Xinyu Wu, Yi Zheng, Jiansong Deng
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21192v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish a geometric dimension criterion for spline spaces on nondegenerate standard Morgan-Scott triangulations with four distinct edge directions at each interior vertex. For every integer $r\ge1$, concurrence of the three auxiliary lines joining corresponding interior and boundary vertices implies that $\dim S_{2r}^r(\Delta_{\mathrm{MS}})$ exceeds the Schumaker lower bound by one. The proof constructs a quadratic form through the six dual spoke points and uses its $r$th power to define a nonzero functional annihilating the image of the smoothing-cofactor map. Diener's upper bound then gives the dimension formula. We also give a matrix representation of this functional and an explicit example in the quadratic case. Combined with the known necessary conditions and the negative-branch exclusion of Deng, Feng, and Kozak, the result yields a necessary and sufficient concurrence criterion for $r>2$.

title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We address an open problem raised by Polyanskiy and Wu in their textbook concerning the subadditivity of mutual \(f\)-information. We study two notions of generalized mutual information: mutual \(f\)-information, defined by \(\widetilde{I}_f(X;Y)=D_f(p_{XY}\|p_Xp_Y)\), and variational \((G,f)\)-information, obtained by minimizing an average of transformed \(f\)-divergences. For the first notion, we derive a sufficient condition on \(g(x)=x^2f''(x)\) that guarantees subadditivity under conditionally independent observations. This condition yields explicit families beyond the previously known examples generated by \(x\log x\) and \((x-1)\log x\). Our proof relies on the concavity of a generalized variance functional. For the variational notion, we extend existing sufficient conditions beyond the transforms \(G(x)\in\{x,\log(1+x),-\log(1-x)\}\). Using a comparison inequality for \(G^{-1}(G(A)+G(B))\), we obtain differential criteria for concave and convex transforms. Explicit constructions illustrate the resulting classes of subadditive information measures.

title: Semisimplicity and Rigidity of the Kontsevich--Zorich Cocycle for Products of Strata
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the Kontsevich--Zorich cocycle, its fixed tensor constructions, and their finite direct sums over products of strata of Abelian differentials. The acting groups are closed subgroups $G\subset(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$ that, up to factor permutations and coordinatewise conjugation by rotations, are products of diagonal $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$ blocks and a finite central group. For ergodic invariant probability measures, we prove Deligne-type semisimplicity: the bundles admit Hodge-compatible decompositions into $G$-invariant pieces $V_i\otimes_{A_i}W_i$, where $A_i$ are division algebras, $V_i$ carry pure variations of Hodge structure, and the multiplicity spaces $W_i$ carry finite direct sums of pure Hodge structures. Every invariant subbundle arises from $A_i$-submodules of the $W_i$.
  If block marginal measures have smooth local supports and are locally equivalent to smooth volume, Hodge-orthogonal projections onto invariant subbundles are locally polynomial in period coordinates on the normalized support. The proof obtains a local product-of-quadrics model and joint polynomiality from polynomiality along stable and unstable leaves. On the cone obtained by scaling each diagonal block together, projection coefficients admit homogeneous degree-zero expressions with integral powers of reciprocal block areas. For the full product group $(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$, single-stratum measure classification supplies the support hypothesis, yielding rigidity for every ergodic invariant probability measure. Under the transported support hypothesis, arbitrary coordinatewise $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$-conjugates also admit polynomial equivariant projectors, though not necessarily Hodge-orthogonal.
  Genus-two examples show that nonrotational conjugation can destroy Deligne-torus invariance, and independent factor scalings can require square roots of area functions.

title: Iterative Bounded Distance Decoding With 2-Bit Reliability Marker For Product-Like Codes
authors: Xiaowei Wu, Min Qiu, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21279v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product codes based on two-bit quantized reliability markers. In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.

title: Dual Representations and Proxy Characterization of $H_2$ Norm for Partial Integral Equations
authors: Danilo Braghini, Tristan Thomas, Sachin Shivakumar, Javad M. Velni, Matthew M. Peet
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21355v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Duality and dual representations are essential tools for systems theory and controller synthesis. For any finite-dimensional causal linear time-invariant (CLTI) system, there exists a dual CLTI system with identical $H_\infty$ and $H_2$ norm. These relations are found by simply taking the adjoint of the transfer function. For nonlinear, time-varying or infinite-dimensional systems, however, such a transfer function may not exist or be difficult to obtain. For duality in the $H_\infty$ norm, this obstacle is overcome by using the equivalent time-domain, induced $L_2$-norm characterization. For $H_2$ norms there is no such equivalent characterization and hence proxy norms such as induced energy to peak and impulse to energy norms are used. These proxy norms bound the $H_2$ norm in the CLTI case. However, neither of these $H_2$ proxy norms equal the same $H_2$ proxy of the canonical dual representation. In this paper, we overcome this by proposing a dual representation whose induced energy to peak proxy equals the impulse to energy proxy of the primal and vice-versa. This relation is developed in the context of Partial Integral Equation (PIE) representations. The result is then used to establish primal-dual operator inequalities for both proxy norms similar in form to the primal-dual LMIs used to characterize the $H_2$ norm.

title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21363v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Test-time scaling can improve the performance of large language models by generating multiple answers to a question and aggregating them. Weighted ensembles extend this idea by drawing answers from several models, with the weights determining how often each model is used. Learning these weights from a training dataset involves two sample sizes: $Q$ labeled questions and $N$ generations per model and question. We study their interplay through the clean risk, the population error of the ensemble's infinite-generation voting rule. Under a margin condition with exponent $\beta$, we show that empirical risk minimization (ERM) with a calibrated margin buffer achieves excess risk of order $Q^{-1/2}+N^{-\beta/2}$, up to logarithmic factors, for fixed numbers of models and candidate answers. To investigate the optimality of this dependence on $Q$ and $N$, we analyze a simplified submodel with two models and two possible answers per question. We characterize its minimax excess risk up to constants by a Hellinger modulus for a binomial-mixture experiment. Polynomial approximation and spectral analysis reveal three regimes. When questions are relatively scarce, the $Q^{-1/2}$ term governs learning and the general buffered ERM is optimal. In an intermediate regime, pooling generation counts across questions improves upon estimating each answer distribution separately, with only logarithmic gains from additional questions. With sufficiently many questions, the minimax excess risk reaches an $N^{-\beta}$ identification floor that persists even with infinitely many questions. The submodel's lower bounds also apply to general ensembles, matching the buffered-ERM upper bound up to logarithmic factors when questions are scarce and in parts of the intermediate regime. Questions remain about the transitions between regimes and the construction of matching pooled estimators for general ensembles.

title: Observability as a constraint qualification for a nonsmooth bilevel PDE-constrained problem
authors: Christian Clason, Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella, Jyrki Jauhiainen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21377v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Motivated by experiment design for parameter identification in image reconstruction, we analyze a bilevel control problem involving sparse inversion at the lower level. Qualified optimality conditions in explicit multiplier form are shown to hold under either an observability condition for a coupled system or the Lebesgue nullity of a contact set induced by the lower-level adjoint variable. We prove that these conditions are independent of one another and that they cannot, in general, both be omitted. The approach is based on the characterization of local first-order geometric objects (tangent and normal cones) associated with a set of lifted constraints. Based on the resulting optimality conditions, we formulate a reduced gradient method and illustrate it through numerical experiments.

title: Optimization of a Perturbed Implicit Sweeping Process by Constrained Discontinuous Controls
authors: Yen Dang, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Dao Nguyen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21384v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies optimal control problems governed by an implicit sweeping process with velocity-dependent constraint geometry, where the dynamics are described by a differential inclusion involving the normal cone to a moving convex polyhedral set. Such systems form a challenging class of nonsmooth differential inclusions due to the implicit coupling between the state, velocity, and constraint reaction. To address these difficulties, we use a method of discrete approximations together with tools of variational analysis and generalized differentiation. This approach allows us to derive necessary optimality conditions for local minimizer in discrete-time problems and subsequently pass to the limit to obtain optimality conditions for the original continuous-time system. The obtained results extend existing optimal control theory for sweeping processes to a class of implicit dynamical systems with state-and velocity-dependent constraints.

title: Kernel-Based Heterogeneous Mean Field Games on a Continuum Type Space
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21423v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies a class of heterogeneous mean field games on a continuum type space, in which interactions are generated by a Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator acting on the type-indexed mean state profile. The control set is allowed to be a general closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, and the optimal feedback is characterized through the unique maximizer of the Hamiltonian. For a prescribed mean-field path, the stochastic maximum principle leads to a family of fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) indexed by the agent type. Under Lipschitz conditions and a monotonicity assumption on the reduced coefficients, the frozen FBSDE is globally well posed. We then formulate the consistency problem as a fixed-point problem for the kernel mean-field path. When the operator norm of the interaction kernel is sufficiently small, the resulting map has an invariant ball and is continuous and compact, so that Schauder's theorem yields existence of a mean field Nash equilibrium. Uniqueness follows under an aggregate monotonicity condition adapted to the kernel coupling. A linear-quadratic example illustrates how finite-rank interactions and heterogeneous risk preferences produce coupled collective modes, and yields a spectral smallness condition for existence and an explicit sufficient condition for uniqueness.

title: Restarted Fixed-Point Acceleration of Proximal ADMM for Capped-$\ell_1$ Penalized Optimization
authors: Hongyuan Tao, Fan Wu, Wei Bian
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21444v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider box-constrained optimization with a convex, Lipschitz continuous loss function that may be nonsmooth and a capped-$\ell_1$ penalty. Exploiting the convex branch representation of the capped-$\ell_1$ penalty, we construct an associated nonexpansive fixed-point mapping for each branch and, based on these mappings, propose a restarted accelerated proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (RA-pADMM). The resulting algorithm consists of a preliminary branch identification phase and a subsequent accelerated phase based on either the Halpern or fast Krasnosel'ski\u{i}--Mann iteration, together with a sufficient decrease restart mechanism. We prove that the preliminary phase terminates after finitely many iterations and that only finitely many branch updates are accepted during the subsequent phase. The primal iterates and proximal outputs converge to a common lifted stationary point, which is also a $\nu$-strong local minimizer of the corresponding cardinality penalized problem. Moreover, the Halpern and fast Krasnosel'ski\u{i}--Mann variants achieve nonergodic $O(k^{-1})$ and asymptotic $o(k^{-1})$ convergence rates, respectively, for both the objective value gap and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker residual associated with the final branch. Numerical experiments on sparse recovery and real data classification problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RA-pADMM algorithm.

title: The Sharp Scale Inequality for the Schatten Trace Class
authors: Yong Jiao, Sijie Luo, Lian Wu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we establish the metric cotype $2$ inequality for the Schatten trace class $S_{1}$ at the optimal order of the scaling parameter. More precisely, for every integer $n\geq 1$, every even integer $m\geq 4$, and every mapping $f:\mathbb{Z}_{m}^{n}\to S_{1}$, the following holds \begin{align*} &\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}_{x}\left\|f\left(x+\frac{m}{2}e_{j}\right)-f(x)\right\|_{1}^{2}\right)^{1/2}\\ \leq&\left(3\sqrt{70}\,m+6\sqrt{n}\right)\left(\mathbb{E}_{x,\varepsilon}\left\|f(x+\varepsilon)-f(x)\right\|_{1}^{2}\right)^{1/2}, \end{align*} where $x$ and $\varepsilon$ are independently uniform on $\mathbb{Z}_{m}^{n}$ and $\{-1,0,1\}^{n}$, respectively. The order $\sqrt{n}$ is necessary for any fixed metric cotype constant. This settles the optimal scaling problem for the Schatten trace class posed by Mendel and Naor \cite[Section 8]{MN} (see also \cite[Question 3]{GMN}).

title: An Alternating Minimization Algorithm for Federated Sparse Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
authors: Yanjiao Zhu, Xianchao Xiu, Yongyang Xiong, Wanquan Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21455v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we develop an alternating minimization algorithm for federated sparse orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization (ONMF) with emphases on controlling client drift. To reduce communication frequency, clients perform multiple local updates between communication rounds, biasing updates toward their respective local objectives and giving rise to client drift, particularly under data heterogeneity. In federated sparse ONMF, global nonsmooth regularization further complicates drift control, as proximal mappings generally do not commute with averaging. To address these challenges, we develop an effective optimization algorithm that introduces variable splitting to decouple proximal operator evaluation from communication, allowing clients to handle joint sparsity regularization locally. In addition, the algorithm incorporates a correction term into the local gradients to adjust the update directions and mitigate client drift. We theoretically establish that the proposed algorithm achieves sublinear convergence to a bounded residual error under some mild conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate favorable convergence behavior on a synthetic dataset and competitive clustering performance on real-world multi-view datasets.

title: Descending Everest with First-Order Oracles: Oracle Complexity of Convex Optimization under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness
authors: Mikhail Rudomanov, Ivan Fomin, Alexander V. Gasnikov, Fedor S. Stonyakin
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions, the curvature may grow together with the gradient norm. Therefore, even when $\|x^0-x^*\|\le R$, the gradient and the optimality gap at the starting point may be exponentially large in $L_1R$, and the bound $\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}$, known for the accelerated method on functions with Lipschitz gradient, no longer describes the complexity of the problem. We determine the oracle complexity of this class for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: for $L_0R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$, the optimal number of oracle calls $N$ satisfies $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1R)$. The upper bound reads $O(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(1+L_1R)\log(2+L_1R))$: the method first passes through the large-gradient regime in $O(1+L_1R)$ iterations with an inexact line search, and then the standard accelerated method with a constant stepsize takes over. The lower bound is obtained by means of chains and the orthogonal invariance principle on functions conjugate to strongly convex functions on a polytope. If the initial optimality gap is at most $4\varepsilon$, the optimal bound becomes $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(L_1R)^{2/3})$.

title: On the structure of polynomial ideal codes and additive Reed--Solomon codes
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study structural properties of polynomial ideal (PI) codes and additive Reed--Solomon (aRS) codes in the folded Hamming metric (equivalently, the Hamming metric over a larger alphabet). We first determine the maximum possible length of PI codes, prove that the dual of every PI code is a generalized PI code, and deduce that PI codes are dually QMDS together with an explicit formula for their weight distribution. We then show that PI codes defined by irreducible polynomials correspond to aRS codes with pairwise nonconjugate evaluation points. For these aRS codes, the previous results on PI codes apply (duality, QMDS property and weight distribution). We show that, asymptotically, aRS codes with nonconjugate evaluation points achieve the same length as PI codes. We also compute the permutation group of such aRS codes. We also extend the family of PI codes to consider arbitrary polynomial modules (not necessarily pairwise coprime), and study when these and general aRS codes satisfy the QMDS and dually QMDS properties.

title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
authors: V. \'Alvarez-Aparicio, J. M. Garc\'{\i}a-Calcines, L. J. Hern\'andez-Paricio, M. T. Rivas-Rodr\'{\i}guez
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21516v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction.
  In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.

title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21536v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

title: Estimators from Convex Geometries of the Simplex
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21551v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We unify several geometries of the probability simplex under one principle, their generation by a potential: convex potentials produce the Bregman divergences and dually flat structures of information geometry, and the exponentially concave potentials of Pal and Wong produce the logarithmic divergences and their projectively flat structures. Each structure carries a duality between maximum entropy and minimum divergence and, with it, a projection principle for estimation: the U-estimators of Eguchi, Komori and Ohara in the first case, the {\lambda}-deformed estimators of Wong and Zhang in the second, both governed by a Pythagorean relation and reducing to maximum likelihood in the undeformed limit. We complete the picture with estimators drawn from the third connection the divergence defines, the Levi-Civita one, by minimizing geodesic distance: existence, uniqueness and influence are then controlled by curvature and diameter rather than by flatness. Along the way the Aitchison geometry appears as the logarithmic-barrier instance of the construction at its critical weight, and the symmetrization of the Pal-Wong transport cost, a smoothing of the Hilbert projective metric, is shown to lose the dual pair and to support instead a Huber-type robust center with bounded influence in a geometry of infinite diameter.

title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By B\'ezivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.

title: Optimal First-Order Methods for a Class of Structured H\"older-Smooth Problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convex optimization with H\"older-continuous gradients has attracted considerable attention as a framework bridging smooth and nonsmooth optimization. For this class, Nesterov's universal fast gradient method attains the optimal black-box complexity, and we study whether exploiting further problem structure can further improve this bound. In this paper, we study an important class of H\"older-smooth problems, namely regularized $\ell_p$ regression with $p\in(1,2)$, whose loss has a $(p-1)$-H\"older-continuous gradient and for which the universal method requires $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2/(3p-2)})$ iterations. Exploiting the problem structure, we characterize a family of smooth approximations based on $p$-Huber smoothing and prove that, for any prescribed smoothness level, it minimizes the worst-case approximation error among smooth lower approximations of the scalar loss. Combined with accelerated proximal gradients, the smoothing approach attains an $\varepsilon$-optimal solution in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1/p})$ matrix--vector products, which significantly improves the complexity guarantee for $1

<2$. We show that this bound is optimal by providing a matching lower bound. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate the practical performance of the proposed methods.

title: A Hybrid High-Order method for variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems with convergence under minimal regularity
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21598v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider a homogeneous Dirichlet problem for nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form with Leray--Lions fluxes of variable growth. The class includes the variable-exponent $p(\cdot)$-Laplacian and regularized Carreau--Yasuda-type laws. We propose and analyze a Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization on general polytopal meshes, a hybrid nonconforming method based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. We develop a variable-exponent polynomial and discrete functional toolkit centered on a mean-exponent norm equivalence, together with inverse, trace, Poincar\'e--Wirtinger, Sobolev--Poincar\'e, discrete Lebesgue embedding, interpolation, and compactness estimates adapted to HHO unknowns. We then establish well-posedness of the nonlinear discrete problem and convergence without assuming additional regularity of the exact solution beyond its natural energy space. The discrete potential converges strongly in every uniformly subcritical variable-exponent Lebesgue space, the reconstructed gradient converges strongly in the natural variable-exponent space, and the stabilization energy vanishes. Numerical experiments in two, three, and four space dimensions confirm convergence for singular solutions and for exponent fields ranging from close to $1$ up to $6$. Quantitative a priori error estimates for the same method are derived in a companion paper.

title: Persistence in probability for stochastic delay equations with multiplicative noise
authors: Mark van den Bosch, John Ioannis Stavroulakis

title: On the stability of basis construction in extended Krylov subspace methods
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21603v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Extended Krylov subspace methods (EKSMs) are a well known approach for approximating the action of a matrix function on a vector $f(A)\mathbf{b}$, and their block versions are often used for solving Lyapunov and Sylvester matrix equations. EKSMs produce Laurent approximations to the underlying operator, which are generally more accurate per iteration than polynomial KSMs, without requiring a pole selection procedure as rational KSMs do. At the same time, due to the expansion of the search space by not only $A$ but also by its inverse, a number of implementation choices must be made that can affect the stability of the algorithm in floating-point arithmetic. We concentrate on two variants that often appear in the literature and in code, based on whether new basis vectors are built via what we denote as ``mixed channels" or ``split channels." We characterize their loss of orthogonality with an easily computable metric and prove that when $A$ is symmetric positive definite, mixed channels have better orthogonality than split channels; however, numerical experiments demonstrate that straightforward predictions are not possible for indefinite or nonsymmetric matrices. We also provide a modular MATLAB toolbox, \texttt{ektoolbox}, that contains new versions of EKSMs with low-synchronization Gram-Schmidt backbones.

title: A priori error estimates for a Hybrid High-Order method on variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21611v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for the Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization of variable-exponent Leray--Lions problems introduced in a companion convergence study. HHO methods belong to the family of hybrid nonconforming methods, based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. Under additional broken regularity of the exact solution and its flux, we establish a localized error estimate that retains the individual element sizes and a global estimate whose rate distinguishes the purely subquadratic, mixed subquadratic--superquadratic, and purely superquadratic regimes. In the subquadratic range, we also derive a regime-dependent refinement that compares the local approximation scale with the local non-degeneracy scale and recovers the optimal polynomial order when that scale is resolved by the mesh. The analysis relies on variable-exponent approximation properties of polynomial projectors, mean-exponent tools for discrete polynomial spaces, and weighted monotonicity estimates. The framework also covers regularized and mildly non-symmetric anisotropic Carreau--Yasuda-type fluxes. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and Voronoi meshes support the predicted rates and show that the regularity assumption on the flux cannot be dispensed with.

title: Greedy multiscale kernel algorithms
authors: Sara Avesani, Armin Iske, Michael Multerer, Tizian Wenzel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multiscale kernel approximation and greedy kernel algorithms are two established tools for scattered data approximation. We combine them into greedy multiscale kernel algorithms, in which every level of a multiscale residual correction is constructed by a greedy kernel algorithm. For the multiscale $f$-greedy algorithm we prove convergence rates in the number of selected centres which coincide (up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent) with the rates of the single-scale $f$-greedy algorithm. The gain of the multiscale construction is in the stability, and we make this precise by a two-sided estimate for the condition number of kernel matrices with rescaled kernels. The lower bound shows that any single-scale method, and in particular the $f$-greedy algorithm, pays for its convergence rate with condition numbers growing at least like a power of the number of centres. In contrast, the multiscale scaling of the kernel keeps this lower bound fixed on every level without changing the rate. The upper bound identifies the separation of the centres at the scale of the kernel as the quantity to control. We give the operation counts of all the methods considered and compare the greedy multiscale algorithms numerically with single-scale greedy and classical multiscale methods, in terms of error, time and conditioning.

title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences.
  We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.

title: Pantograph Difference Equations: Stability, Multistability, and Chaos
abstract:
arXiv:2610.21635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pantograph equations are functional differential equations with proportional delay, typically involving terms of the form $x(at)$, where $0<a><1$. These equations have been studied for several decades and have applications in areas ranging from number theory to electrodynamics. In this work, we investigate pantograph difference equations as discrete dynamical maps of the form \[ x_{i+1}=F(x_{i})+G(x_{h(i)}), \qquad i\geq 0, \] where $h(i)\leq i$. In particular, we consider $h(i)=\lfloor ai \rfloor$ and $h(i)=\lfloor ai^{\alpha}\rfloor$, with $0<a><1$ and $0<\alpha<1$. We distinguish between homogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)=0$, and inhomogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)\ne 0$. We first analyze linear pantograph difference equations and establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and for nonconvergence to zero. For proportional delays, analytical stability and instability regions are combined with multi-horizon parameter scans to construct regime diagrams in the $(\lambda,\delta)$-plane. We then investigate pantograph versions of the logistic and tent maps. In the homogeneous case, the dynamics evolves through step-like plateaus whose lengths increase at least exponentially, leading to slow convergence and finite-time multistability within computationally accessible time scales. In the inhomogeneous case, numerical experiments show finite-time exponential separation of nearby trajectories, consistent with chaotic dynamics.
